tool-name.purpose: A tool's name in its featured field on the index, extra-bold at -0.04em: 40px on phones, 60 from 640 while stacked, 36 from 1024 with three side by side, 48 from 1280. The largest type on the index at every width.

index-name.purpose: Flint, the index's h1, one step below the tools' names: 36px on phones, 48 from 640, 36 from 768, 30 from 1024, 36 from 1280.

lead-line.purpose: Flint's muted line beside its name, and what a tool does, in its featured field.

stays-heading.purpose: "Nothing else leaves" under the featured fields, and "All tools" over the A-to-Z list there.

fact.purpose: What leaves a tool, in its featured field, and the three facts under the fields.

start.purpose: The label of a featured field's pink start, bold, never wrapping.

nav.purpose: The header's links to the featured tools, a tool's name in a row of tools, and a kind's name on QR code's shelf.

minor-heading.purpose: The heading of the tools on sites of their own, under the facts.

body.purpose: A tool's introduction under its title, and running prose.

leaves-heading.purpose: "What leaves it" in each featured field, and "Opened lately" and "A to Z" in All tools; bold and muted.

control.purpose: Field text, chips, notes, hints, amounts and the shared bill's line; 16px on touch screens for fields.

label.purpose: Field labels, secondary and small button labels.

tool-title.purpose: A tool's name at the top of its page, extra-bold at -0.04em like its name in its featured field: 36px on phones, 48 from 640, under the tool's symbol.

part-heading.purpose: Split bill's parts, "Your link", "Your code", a picked QR kind and the All tools dialog's heading, extra-bold at -0.03em. A count beside it is muted and regular weight.

step-tab.purpose: The three steps' names in Split bill's step bar, semibold, never wrapping; 13px below 400 px wide.

shadows.name: floating-list
shadows.purpose: The open list of SearchableSelect, and anything else that floats. Nothing else.

motion.name: hover-colors
motion.purpose: Color, opacity and fill changes on hover.

motion.name: arrow-nudge
motion.purpose: The drawn arrow on an action line or link, on hover.

motion.name: theme-cross-fade
motion.value: document.startViewTransition on a theme change, no-preference only
motion.purpose: When someone picks a theme in the footer, or the device switches under System.

motion.name: show-it-outline
motion.purpose: The item "Show it" points to in Split bill, then fades back.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one main action in a view: pastel pink, graphite text.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary">Copy link</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:.5rem;border:1px solid var(--accent-edge);border-radius:9999px;background:var(--accent);color:var(--on-accent);padding:.75rem 1.5rem;font:600 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;cursor:pointer;transition:opacity .15s}.ds-btn-primary:hover{opacity:.85}.ds-btn-primary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px}.ds-btn-primary:disabled{opacity:.5;cursor:not-allowed}

components.name: Start
components.description: A featured field's pink start on the index: the primary button at the field's scale, one per featured field, never wrapping, at the bottom of the field side by side. Its edge and focus follow the field's ground (shown here in the first, inverse field on a light page).
components.html: Split a bill
components.css: .ds-start-field{--bg:#2b2b2b;--text:#f2f2f2;--muted:#aaaaaa;--accent:#febfca;--on-accent:#2b2b2b;--accent-edge:#febfca;--accent-text:#febfca;--focus:#febfca;--control-border:#8a8a8a;background:var(--bg);color:var(--text);padding:1.5rem}.ds-start{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;white-space:nowrap;border:1px solid var(--accent-edge);border-radius:9999px;background:var(--accent);color:var(--on-accent);padding:1rem 1.75rem;font:700 1.125rem/1.55 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;text-decoration:none;transition:opacity .15s}.ds-start:hover{opacity:.85}.ds-start:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px;border-radius:9999px}

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Every other action beside the primary: a transparent pill with a 3:1 edge.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-secondary">Copy as text</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:.5rem;border:1px solid var(--control-border);border-radius:9999px;background:transparent;color:var(--text);padding:.75rem 1.5rem;font:500 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color .15s}.ds-btn-secondary:hover{background:var(--bg)}.ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Small Button
components.description: Actions inside a part, "Next" before a step's work has started, "Add a message" on WhatsApp click-to-chat, "All tools" and "Close" in the header's dialog, and the update notice.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-small">Next</button>
components.css: .ds-btn-small{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;min-height:2.25rem;border:1px solid var(--control-border);border-radius:9999px;background:transparent;color:var(--text);padding:0 1rem;font:500 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color .15s}.ds-btn-small:hover{background:var(--bg)}.ds-btn-small:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px}@media (pointer:coarse){.ds-btn-small{min-height:2.75rem}}

components.name: Field
components.description: A labelled text field on the page itself, filled with the page color and shaped by its control edge.
components.html: <label class="ds-label" for="ds-f">Phone number</label><input id="ds-f" class="ds-field" placeholder="0812-xxxx-xxxx">
components.css: .ds-label{display:block;margin-bottom:.375rem;font:500 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--text)}.ds-field{width:100%;border:1px solid var(--control-border);border-radius:.5rem;background:var(--bg);color:var(--text);padding:.625rem .75rem;font:400 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-field::placeholder{color:var(--muted)}.ds-field:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px}@media (pointer:coarse){.ds-field{font-size:1rem}}

components.name: Tag Chips
components.description: People on a bill, tapped to say who had what. Selected is pink with a check mark.
components.css: .ds-chips{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:.5rem}.ds-chip{min-height:2.25rem;border:1px solid var(--control-border);border-radius:9999px;background:transparent;color:var(--text);padding:0 .875rem;font:400 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color .15s}.ds-chip:hover{background:var(--surface)}.ds-chip-on,.ds-chip-on:hover{border-color:var(--accent-edge);background:var(--accent);color:var(--on-accent);font-weight:500}.ds-chip:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px}@media (pointer:coarse){.ds-chip{min-height:2.75rem}}

components.name: Featured Fields
components.description: The index: the featured tools as full-bleed, square-edged fields in a row between two hairlines, side by side from 1024px and stacked below. Tones go by position: the first is the page's inverse (graphite with dark colors on a light page, shown), the second paper elevated (graphite surface on a dark page), the third the page itself. Names lead at poster scale, each with what leaves it and one pink start.
components.html:
Split bill

Tag who had what; tax and service included.

What leaves it

Only a bill you share, encrypted. Deleted 30 days after the last share.

Split a bill

WhatsApp click‑to‑chat

Message a number without saving it.

What leaves it

A chat you open, sent to WhatsApp with the number and message you typed.

Chat with a number

QR code

A code for a link, a Wi-Fi network or a contact.

What leaves it

Nothing. The code is made on your device, and the file stays there.

Make a code

components.name: Tool Symbol
components.description: Each tool's one fixed symbol, a 4-unit stroke on a 40-unit square in the text color: a half-filled circle for Split bill, a speech mark for WhatsApp, three corner squares and a module for QR code, a picture's frame, hills and sun for Resize and convert images. 1.25rem in the header and rows, 2rem in a field on phones and 2.5rem from 640px.
components.css: .ds-syms{display:flex;gap:1.5rem;color:var(--text)}.ds-syms .ds-sym{width:2.5rem;height:2.5rem}

components.name: Part
components.description: A part of Split bill, with no card: an extra-bold heading, its content on the page, and a hairline to the next part. Items are rows between hairlines.
components.html:
Items (2)

  • Nasi Goreng Rp 45.000
  • Es Teh Rp 12.000

Charges and adjustments
components.css: .ds-parts{font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--text)}.ds-part{padding:2rem 0}.ds-part:first-child{padding-top:0}.ds-part+.ds-part{border-top:1px solid var(--border)}.ds-part-h{margin:0 0 1rem;font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:800;line-height:1.33;letter-spacing:-.03em}.ds-part-h span{font-weight:400;color:var(--muted)}.ds-rows{margin:.5rem 0 0;padding:0;list-style:none}.ds-rows li{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;padding:1rem 0;font-size:.875rem}.ds-rows li+li{border-top:1px solid var(--border)}

components.name: Note
components.description: An aside to act on now, marked by a pink edge all round.
components.html: The items add up to Rp 12.000 less than the receipt's subtotal. Check the marked prices.
components.css: .ds-note{border:1px solid var(--accent-edge);border-radius:.5rem;background:var(--bg);color:var(--text);padding:.75rem;font:400 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}

components.name: Step Bar
components.description: Split bill's three plain tabs below 1024px. The current one is in the text color with a 3px underline in the text color on a 1px hairline; the others are muted. aria-current="step"; any order, no numbers, no pink.
components.css: .ds-steps{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:.25rem;margin:0;padding:0;list-style:none;border-bottom:1px solid var(--border);white-space:nowrap;font:600 .8125rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-step{display:flex;align-items:center;min-height:2.75rem;margin-bottom:-1px;padding:0 .25rem;border:0;border-bottom:3px solid transparent;background:none;color:var(--muted);font:inherit;cursor:pointer}.ds-step:hover{color:var(--text)}.ds-step[aria-current=step]{color:var(--text);border-bottom-color:var(--text)}.ds-step:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px;border-radius:4px}@media (min-width:400px){.ds-steps{font-size:.875rem}}

components.name: Bottom Bar
components.description: Split bill's bar fixed to the bottom of a phone's screen on steps 1 and 2: graphite with dark mode's colors on a light page, graphite surface on a dark one. The step's count or the total and what's in nobody's share, and "Next", outlined until the step's work has started, then pink.
components.html:
Total
Rp 486.200
Not in anyone's share yet
Rp 35.000
components.css: .ds-bar{--surface:#2b2b2b;--bg:#2b2b2b;--border:#474747;--text:#f2f2f2;--muted:#aaaaaa;--accent:#febfca;--on-accent:#2b2b2b;--accent-edge:#febfca;--focus:#febfca;--control-border:#8a8a8a;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:.75rem;background:var(--surface);color:var(--text);padding:.75rem 1.25rem;font:400 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-bar dl{margin:0}.ds-bar dl div{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:0 .375rem}.ds-bar dd{margin:0;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}.ds-bar-next{flex-shrink:0;white-space:nowrap;border:1px solid var(--accent-edge);border-radius:9999px;background:var(--accent);color:var(--on-accent);padding:.75rem 1.5rem;font:600 .875rem/1.43 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;cursor:pointer;transition:opacity .15s}.ds-bar-next:hover{opacity:.85}.ds-bar-next:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Tool Title
components.description: A tool page's title, said as its field on the index says it: the tool's symbol, its name in extra-bold tool-title type, and the introduction under it. No band, nothing above the symbol. Used by every tool.
components.html:
Split bill

Tag who had what, and we work out a fair share for each person, tax and service included.
components.css: .ds-tool-title{font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--text)}.ds-tt-sym{display:block;width:1.75rem;height:1.75rem}.ds-tt-name{margin:.75rem 0 0;font-size:2.25rem;font-weight:800;line-height:.95;letter-spacing:-.04em}.ds-tt-intro{margin:.75rem 0 0;max-width:36rem;line-height:1.625;color:var(--muted)}@media (min-width:640px){.ds-tt-sym{width:2rem;height:2rem}.ds-tt-name{font-size:3rem}}

components.name: Your Code
components.description: QR code's answer: the bare code, graphite on a white sheet with a hairline and square corners in both themes, its margin part of the drawing, beside "Your code" and what scanning it does; then Save as PNG (pink) and Save as SVG side by side, and a status line kept under them.
components.html:
Your code

Opens the website itrium.id. Scan it once before you print it.

Look for qr-code-itrium.id.png in your downloads.
components.css: .ds-code{font-family:'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;color:var(--text)}.ds-cwrap{display:flex;align-items:flex-start;gap:1.25rem}.ds-sheet{width:9.5rem;flex-shrink:0;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:0;background:#ffffff}.ds-sheet svg{display:block;width:100%}.ds-ch{margin:0 0 .5rem;font-size:1.5rem;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:-.03em;line-height:1.33}.ds-cl{margin:0;font-size:.875rem;line-height:1.625;color:var(--muted)}.ds-saves{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:.75rem;margin-top:1.25rem}.ds-png,.ds-svg{flex-grow:1;white-space:nowrap;border-radius:9999px;padding:.875rem 1rem;font:600 1rem/1.5 'Plus Jakarta Sans Variable',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;cursor:pointer}.ds-png{border:1px solid var(--accent-edge);background:var(--accent);color:var(--on-accent);transition:opacity .15s}.ds-png:hover{opacity:.85}.ds-svg{border:1px solid var(--control-border);background:transparent;color:var(--text);font-weight:500;transition:background-color .15s}.ds-svg:hover{background:var(--elevated,#f1f1f1)}.ds-png[aria-disabled=true],.ds-svg[aria-disabled=true]{opacity:.5;cursor:not-allowed}.ds-png:focus-visible,.ds-svg:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:3px}.ds-status{margin:.75rem 0 0;min-height:2.5rem;font-size:.875rem}@media (min-width:1024px){.ds-sheet{width:16rem}.ds-cwrap{gap:2rem}}

components.name: Kind Shelf
components.description: QR code's other kinds, quiet under the answer: a small extra-bold heading, then rows between hairlines, each kind's name semibold and underlined at rest, what it's for muted on the right. Picking one swaps its fields into the first part. Never pink.
components.html: Something other than a link

components.name: Segmented Pills
components.description: A choice among a few short options (a unit, a format, the theme), drawn as the footer's theme choice: one pill-edged group with a control edge, the chosen option filled in the text color and semibold. Never pink. 2.25rem options (2.75rem on touch), narrower padding below 25rem so four fit at 360px; a wrapping group eases to 1.5rem corners.
components.html: Save as

components.name: Your Images
components.description: Resize and convert images' answer: rows between hairlines, each at least 7.25rem tall (7.75rem on touch): a 3.5rem tile, the name in semibold, "before → after · W × H" with the after in semibold, notes for finished rows only (the drawn warning sign for something to check; a plain muted line for "no details to keep"), and Save (aria-disabled until done) and Remove on the right. components.name: Update Notice
components.description: The offer of a new version, over the header at the top of the page: surface fill, a control-edge border, 1rem corners, no shadow, and an outlined small Update button.
components.html: A new version of Flint is ready.

components.name: Navigation
components.description: The header on every page: the pink stone mark with no tile and "Flint" on the left; the featured tools as direct links from 1024px (current page underlined) and the small "All tools" button on the right.
components.html:
Flint
  • Split bill

narrative.northStar: The Rhodonite Specimen, put to work
narrative.overview:
The tools are cut from the same stone as itrium.id. That site is The Rhodonite Specimen (`DESIGN.md` in the `website` repository): a graphite matrix with a pink vein, where gray is the body and pink marks what a visitor should find. Here the specimen leaves the display case and goes onto the workbench. The world is the same: Plus Jakarta Sans for everything, graphite and paper, pastel pink with its two deepenings, flat tonal surfaces, pills and soft corners, one drawn arrow. Only the job changes. itrium.id persuades; a tool gets out of the way.

The index is Featured, then the rest: the featured tools (three, `FEATURED_COUNT` in `src/lib/tools.ts`) as full-bleed fields laid edge to edge, side by side from 1024px and stacked below it. No metaphor, no cards, no rounded boxes: the fields are the page. They have square edges and are told apart by tone alone. The first is always the inverse of the page (graphite on a light page, paper elevated on a dark one), the second a tonal step off the page, and the third the page itself, held between the row's two hairlines. Each field carries its tool's symbol, its name at poster scale, what it does, what leaves it, and one large pink start. Flint's name, its line and a search for a tool sit above them, a step below the tools' names, and what never leaves sits on the page below. Once there are more tools than fields, every tool follows A to Z: a plain list while each letter holds one tool, under initials once a letter holds two. It replaced Two halves (two tools, one seam), which replaced the Rantang (#73), the Device Map (#71) and the line-item strip (#70).

Every page's header holds Flint's mark and name, the featured tools as direct links from 1024px, and "All tools", one button that opens every tool with a search by name or task, the ones opened lately on this device first. Switching tools stays one press and a word away however many there are.

A tool page follows the index. It opens with the tool's title, said as its field says it: the tool's symbol and its name in the same extra-bold type, the introduction under it. All four tools are drawn in this world, with no cards. Split bill's parts are divided by plain lines under extra-bold headings, items as rows between lines, and below 1024px the bill is made in three steps, one on screen at a time, with a graphite bar fixed to the bottom of the screen holding the step's count or total and the way on. The person using it is at a restaurant table with a phone in one hand and a group waiting, so they do one job at a time and the answer is one tap away. WhatsApp click-to-chat is the fields, then under a plain line the answer: "Your link", what it opens, a way to make a QR code for the number, and "Open in WhatsApp" and "Copy link". QR code is a link or any text, then under a plain line the bare code beside "Your code", redrawn as it's typed, its two saves, and a short shelf of other kinds (Wi-Fi, contact, email, phone call) whose fields take the first part's place when picked. From 1024px each tool's answer has its own column.

Components are soft and sure-footed, and tactile without being playful. Every control has a round, generous target that a thumb finds the first time (2.75rem on touch screens) and an edge you can see (3:1 against every surface they sit on). They feel good to press but never perform. Density on the index is bold and wide; inside a tool it is calm and working: below 1024px forms sit in a narrow column of 36 to 42rem, from 1024px a tool takes the 72rem column with its answer beside the form, and the few things that really are boxes (receipt lines, the adjustments list, a note) sit one step back with a hairline round them.

Light and dark are equal. Each follows the visitor's system unless the footer says otherwise, and neither is a courtesy version of the other: every new pairing is designed and checked in both. The system refuses what itrium.id refuses: generic SaaS ornament (gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers), drop shadows on anything but a floating list, pure black and white, decorative pink, and small labels above headings. It refuses what only a tool can get wrong: a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen, and state shown by color alone. And on the index it refuses what the owner has turned down four times over: anything that reads as a receipt (dashed lines, gray-on-paper monochrome, a narrow column, rows of entries), any metaphor (a map, a food carrier), and a column of stacked rounded boxes. On Split bill the owner turned down the same stack: "too many boxes".
keyCharacteristics: One stone with itrium.id: the same tokens, typeface, radii, button shapes and arrow.
The index leads with the featured tools as full-bleed fields, square-edged, side by side from 1024px and stacked below, their content lined up with the header's 72rem column.
The first field is the inverse of the page in both themes, the second a tonal step off it, the third the page itself between the row's hairlines.
The tools' names lead the page at every width, a step above Flint's own name.
Each tool has one fixed symbol, drawn in the text color, the same in the header, in "All tools", in its field and over its title.
Pink only at the featured fields' starts on the index (equal starts), and at one primary action per tool view.
The header is the mark, the featured tools from 1024px, and "All tools": a dialog with a search, "Opened lately" and A to Z.
A tool page opens with its title: the tool's symbol and its name in extra-bold type, as in its field, and the introduction under it.
Split bill has no cards: parts between plain lines, items as rows, three steps below 1024px with a graphite bar at the bottom, and two columns from 1024px.

WhatsApp click-to-chat, QR code and Resize and convert images have no card: the fields, a plain line, then the answer, in its own column beside a vertical line from 1024px. Only QR code draws a code, bare, on a white sheet.
Light and dark are equal. Both follow the system, unless System, Light or Dark is chosen in the footer.
Flat surfaces with tonal steps. The only shadow is under the open searchable list; "All tools" is set apart by its backdrop, not a shadow.
Every control has a 3:1 edge (`--control-border`), a target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens, and 16px text on touch screens so iOS doesn't zoom.
Motion is CSS only and off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Vein Rule
rules.body: Pink marks something: the primary action, focus, what's selected, or the way onward. If you can't say what a pink element marks, it should be gray. Pink means one thing at a time, which is not the same as one element. In a tool, one pink button per view. On the index, one pink start in each featured field, the tools' equal starts ("Split a bill", "Chat with a number", "Make a code"): one meaning, three pills. Rose-text action lines serve the tools elsewhere, a shared bill and WhatsApp's hand-off to QR code as their way onward, and nothing else is pink but the mark. The fields, the search, "All tools", the tool symbols, a tool's title, the step bar, the shelf and the code are never pink. On Split bill below 1024px the bar's "Next" counts toward the view: it is outlined until the step's own work has started (nobody added on step 1, nothing on the bill on step 2), so the step's own pink action ("Scan or paste a receipt") isn't doubled.

rules.name: The Inverse Field Rule
rules.body: The index's first featured field (the `.inverse-field` scope) takes the colors of the theme the page is not in, every one of them: on a light page graphite, with off-white text, muted gray on dark, pink focus, pink edges and pink text, and the dark control edge; on a dark page paper elevated, with graphite text, muted gray on light, deep-rose edges, rose text, graphite focus, and the light control edge. Nothing inside it reads the page's own colors. The owner chose this on 2026-11-24 and accepted its cost: a bright band across a dark page, in exchange for fields told apart strongly in both themes. The second field takes the page's own colors on a step off it (paper elevated, or graphite surface on a dark page), and the third is the page. The contrast for each pairing is in the comment above the scope in `src/app.css`.

rules.name: The Graphite Bar Rule
rules.body: Split bill's bar at the bottom of a phone's screen is graphite on a light page, with every color inside it from dark mode (the `.graphite-bar` scope: off-white text, pink focus and edges, the dark control edge), like the first featured field. On a dark page it does not invert: it stays dark, a step up to graphite surface, because a bright band held under the thumb at a dim table is too much.

rules.name: The Two Borders Rule
rules.body: `--border` is for lines nothing depends on, such as dividing lines and the edges of inset lists, the code's sheet and the "All tools" panel. Anything a person has to find in order to use it gets `--control-border`.

rules.name: The Graphite Text Rule
rules.body: Text on pink is graphite, never white. On light backgrounds pink text is rose text and pink lines are deep rose. Pastel pink is never text or a line there. A checked box or radio button takes the text color, not pink, so it never competes with the next action.

rules.name: The Every-Surface Rule
rules.body: Contrast is checked on every surface text sits on: page, inset list, note, the bottom bar, update notice, the "All tools" panel, the error page's panel, and each featured field in both themes. Text needs 4.5:1. Focus outlines, control edges and state lines need 3:1. The tightest are the first featured field on a light page (control edge 3.7:1) and on a dark page (muted 4.7:1, rose text 4.8:1).

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Plus Jakarta Sans does everything. Never add a second family, and never load a font from another domain.

rules.name: The Tools Lead Rule
rules.body: On the index, the tools' names are the largest type at every width, and Flint's own name steps down with them: 40 over 36 on phones, 60 over 48 from 640 px, 60 over 36 from 768 px, 36 over 30 from 1024 px, 48 over 36 from 1280 px. A new size for one is a new size for the other. From 1024 px the names are sized so the longest word ("click-to-chat") fits a third of the column. On a tool page the tool's title is the largest type, in the same extra-bold voice.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: A heading is the first thing in its block. No eyebrow, category label, small uppercase heading or back link sits above it. Nothing here is set in uppercase. A line that says more about a heading goes under it or beside it, as Flint's line does. A field's symbol sits above the tool's name, but it is the tool's picture, not a label; an A-to-Z initial sits beside or above the names it groups, and is hidden from screen readers.

rules.name: The Featured Fields Rule
rules.body: The index leads with the featured tools, one full-bleed field each, side by side from 1024 px and told apart by tone. A field holds its tool's symbol, name, what it does, what leaves it and its own pink start, and nothing else. No cards inside or around them, no hero over them, no column of boxes. Every other tool waits in the A-to-Z list under them and in "All tools", never as a smaller field or a card.

rules.name: The Kept Space Rule
rules.body: What the browser remembers arrives into a space already kept for it (what Split bill does keeps two lines, 2.75em; the shared bill's line keeps 3rem, `kept-line`; side by side every field keeps both), so nothing moves under a finger when it appears. The same holds inside a tool: the code's empty sheet keeps its place, the line under a number and the note under "Link or text" keep two lines (`note-slot`), Save as PNG and Save as SVG are there before there's a code, the status line under them keeps two lines, and "Copy link" keeps its width when it says "Copied". On Resize and convert images, the details box's line is one line either way, a row's Save is there from its first frame, every row keeps room for one note, and the status line is kept before anything is saved.

rules.name: The Slab Rule, for tools
rules.body: A tool page has no slab at either end: it opens with the tool's title, its symbol and its name, and never closes with a panel. On a phone, the tool comes before the frame.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Below 1024px Split bill shows one step at a time, and the steps are free: any tab, in any order. Whatever a control sends focus to brings its own step on screen first (`focusAfter`), so "Show it" from the split lands on the item in step 2. A step is a view, not a gate: nothing is removed from the page, and nothing is checked before moving on.

rules.name: The First Screen Rule
rules.body: On a phone, the first field of a tool is visible without scrolling, and on the index Split bill's start is; from 1024 px every featured field's start is. If a new element would push any of them down, it belongs lower on the page.

rules.name: The Answer In Reach Rule
rules.body: Wherever a tool is being filled in, its answer is one glance or one tap away: the step bar and the bottom bar's total below 1024 px, the split's own column above; on WhatsApp click-to-chat, the line reading the number back under its field, and the answer right under the fields, nothing floating over it. Someone opening a shared result lands on it, not on the form that made it.

rules.name: The Only Floating Things Cast Shadows Rule
rules.body: Featured fields, buttons, chips, the "All tools" panel, the error page's panel, the code's sheet and the bottom bar never get a drop shadow. A control responds by filling with the next tonal step, a header link by its underline, and an arrow by moving 4 px on.

rules.name: The Square Field Rule
rules.body: The featured fields have square edges and meet on straight lines. No arcs, rails, rims, dashes or shadows on the index.

rules.name: The Pinned Fact Rule
rules.body: What leaves a tool is said in that tool's field, above its start, before anyone presses it, and again beside it in the A-to-Z list. What never leaves is said once, under the fields. Never collect them into a legend or a list apart from the tools they concern.

rules.name: The Peer Rule
rules.body: The featured fields are equal: the same type, the same rhythm, the same size of start. No tool is a hero over the others; the inverse tone goes to the first field only so the fields read apart, not to rank it.

rules.name: The Whole Edge Rule
rules.body: A note is marked by its whole edge, never by a thick bar down one side.

rules.name: The One Pink Save Rule
rules.body: On Resize and convert images the only pink is "Save all". The size's unit, the format, a row's Save and "Add images" are graphite or outlined, however much they're used.

dos: **Do** take tokens, radii, button shapes, the arrow and type roles from itrium.id's DESIGN.md before inventing anything. A difference between the two sites needs a reason a tool has and a page doesn't.

**Do** add a new tool to the registry (`src/lib/tools.ts`) once: its name, short name, line, what leaves it, its start and its search words. The index's fields, its A-to-Z list, the header and "All tools" all read from there.

**Do** keep the first featured field the inverse of the page in both themes, with every color inside it from the other theme (`.inverse-field`), the second a tonal step off the page and the third the page between hairlines; and check each pairing when one is added.
**Do** keep the tools' names a step above Flint's at every width, and each name two lines tall side by side, so the fields' lines meet across them.
**Do** give every tool one symbol and use it wherever the tool is named in the frame: the header, a row in a list of tools, its field and its title.
**Do** keep a tool's first field, and Split bill's start on the index, on the first phone screen, and every featured start on the first screen at 1024 by 768, 1280 by 800 and 1440 by 900.

**Do** list tools as rows between hairlines (symbol, name, what it does), the same in the index's search, "All tools" and the A-to-Z list; and keep "Opened lately" by recency, ids only, on the device.
**Do** keep a slot for what may appear (a note under a field, a status line under saves, a button that can't act yet) before it appears, so nothing moves under a finger.
**Do** give every field, button and chip a `--control-border` edge and a touch target at least 2.75rem tall on touch screens.

**Do** show every state in two ways: a check mark with the pink fill, words with the pink edge, an underline on the current page's link, and the reason a button can't be pressed yet, said under it when someone presses or reaches it (not at rest, and not read out again after every add).
**Do** design and check every new pairing in light and dark, on every surface it sits on, at level AA.
**Do** hand a value from one tool to another after the `#`, which never reaches a server, and take it out of the address once it's read.
**Do** draw a choice among a few short options (a unit, a format, the theme) as the footer's segmented pills: one pill-edged group, the chosen option filled in the text color.
**Do** keep a row's height steady while its work is redone: room for its actions and one note from the first frame, and "Working…" in place of the result, not a spinner over it.
**Do** use the drawn arrow wherever a link points onward.

**Do** keep motion in CSS, gated on `motion-safe` or `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`: page cross-fades, the theme cross-fade (a view transition, when someone picks a theme or the device switches under System), the 4 px arrow nudge, and the loading spinner. Nothing rises or reveals as it scrolls.
**Do** open a tool page with its title: its symbol, its name in extra-bold tool-title type, and the introduction under it, lined up with the header and the tool.
**Do** divide a tool's parts with plain hairlines under extra-bold part headings, and set items as rows between lines; keep a box only for a list checked line by line or a note asking for attention.
**Do** keep every step of Split bill in the page, shown or hidden by its step, and bring a step on screen before focusing anything in it.
**Do** count the bottom bar's "Next" in a view's one pink action: outlined until the step's own work has started.
**Do** use Tailwind classes with the theme tokens and the shared classes in `src/lib/styles.ts`, never raw hex values in markup.
donts: **Don't** make the index read as a receipt, on any cue: no dashed lines, no gray-on-paper monochrome, no narrow column, no rows of entries as its front door. The owner turned down the line-item strip (#70) and the Device Map (#71) for exactly this. Rows belong to finding a tool (the search's answers, the A-to-Z list under the fields), never in place of the fields.
**Don't** give the index a metaphor: no map, no food carrier, no object for the tools to sit in. The owner turned down the Device Map (#71) and the Rantang (#73) for this.
**Don't** draw the index as a column of stacked rounded boxes, or put cards, a legend or a hero over the featured fields; a tool beyond them is a row, never a smaller field or a card.
**Don't** round the featured fields, inset them from the screen's edges, or draw an arc, rail, rim, dash or shadow on the index.

**Don't** use pink as decoration, or give pink two meanings in one view: a tool has one pink button, and the index's starts are all the primary action, one in each featured field. The fields, the search, "All tools", the shelf, the code and the symbols are never pink.
**Don't** list every tool in the header: it holds the featured ones from 1024 px and "All tools".

**Don't** add a structural gray outside the palette. Its one exception, the error panel's raised border in dark mode (#4f4f4f), is a structural step above a palette gray; a new one needs the same reason, and a color change otherwise belongs in `@itrium/palettes`.
**Don't** put a small uppercase heading, eyebrow, kicker or back link above a heading.
**Don't** type arrows or chevrons as characters.
**Don't** give featured fields, buttons, chips, the "All tools" panel, the code's sheet, the error panel or the bottom bar a drop shadow.
**Don't** put Split bill's parts back in cards, or stack rounded boxes in a tool: the owner turned that down as "too many boxes".

**Don't** put WhatsApp click-to-chat back in a card, draw a code on it again (it hands its link to QR code), put its message in a code it hands over, draw a dashed road under its actions, or show its link as raw monospace text.
**Don't** put QR code's kinds in tabs above the main job, add words to the saved image, route a code through anything in between, or hide the code behind a disclosure.
**Don't** fill a chosen segmented pill in pink, show a note for settings that are being redone, or put the warning sign on a fact that isn't a problem ("no details to keep").
**Don't** gate Split bill's steps, number them, or mark one done: they are free, in any order.
**Don't** invert the bottom bar on a dark page: it stays dark.
**Don't** use `#000000` or pure white text on pink. Graphite is `#2b2b2b`.
**Don't** put pastel pink text or lines on a light background, including the first featured field on a dark page; or rose text and deep-rose lines on graphite, including that field on a light page.
**Don't** use a native `<select>`, inline styles, `data:` URLs, or anything from another domain.
**Don't** add gradient text, icon-card rows, invented numbers, or a hero that pushes the tool off a phone screen.
**Don't** set field text below 16px on touch screens.
**Don't** put a band behind a tool's title: the band is the error page's alone.
